notes: The large red box clearly shows a resting camel with a decorated saddle blanket. The smaller red box shows part of another camel's saddle and body in the background. Neither blue box contains a camel: one shows the tent with a lantern, the other the starry sky. A third camel at left-center falls outside both boxes, so tapping it would count as neither right nor wrong.

The red box contains the tent with its open entrance, framed by poles and fringed drapes, with a lantern and firelight visible inside. The blue boxes contain the starry sky, a resting camel, and saddled camels, with no tent door in any of them.

The red box clearly shows a dense starry night sky with the Milky Way. However, the left blue box (tent) extends into the upper sky above and beside the tent, where some scattered stars are also visible, so the same kind of object appears in a wrong-answer region. The camel boxes mainly show mountains and terrain, with little or no sky.

The red box contains the central robed figure standing in the boat with an outstretched arm toward the storm, which is recognisable as Jesus rebuking the wind. The blue boxes show crashing waves and the boat's hull with a disciple's arm; none of them contain the Jesus figure.

The red box clearly contains the ocean: large waves with sunlight reflecting on the water. The blue boxes show the starry sky with clouds, the moon, the sun at the horizon and an orange tree. The sun box touches the horizon but mainly shows the sun and sky, not the sea.

The 'lesser light to rule the night' (Genesis 1:16) is the moon. The red box clearly shows a full moon. The blue boxes contain the starry sky (the stars are mentioned separately in that verse, not the lesser light), the sun (the greater light), the ocean waves and a fruit tree. None of them contains a moon.

The 'greater light to rule the day' is the sun. The red box clearly shows the sun setting on the horizon. The blue boxes contain the moon (the lesser light), stars, the sea, and a fruit tree. None of them shows the sun itself. The sea box has only the sun's reflection, not the sun.

The red box contains the wooden hull of the boat, with its planks, rope, and gunwale, which an adult would recognise as the disciples' boat. The left blue box shows crashing waves, possibly with a sliver of the hull edge at its right margin. The center blue box shows the Jesus figure, with only a small part of the hull at its bottom edge. Neither blue box clearly contains a ship.

The red box contains a tree bearing many orange-red fruits, so the fruit tree is clearly visible. The blue boxes contain the starry sky with clouds, the moon, the setting sun and the ocean waves; none contains a fruit tree.

The red box contains an elderly bearded man in robes standing in a lions' den, a clear depiction of Daniel. The blue boxes show the light shaft at the cave opening and a resting male lion with a lioness. Neither contains a human figure, so neither shows Daniel.

The red box contains the large male lion with a full, great mane, lying down with closed eyes. One blue box holds the robed old man; the other holds the light shaft and opening in the cave ceiling. Neither blue box contains a maned lion. The edge of the man's box overlaps a small part of a lioness, which has no mane.

The red box clearly shows a dark night sky dotted with many bright stars. The blue boxes contain the moon, the sun, ocean waves and an orange tree. The moon box and the tree box may include a few faint specks of sky, but neither clearly features stars.

The red box frames the bright opening in the cave ceiling, with sunlight and vines spilling through, so the opening at the top of the den is clearly visible there. One blue box contains the man and the other contains the lions. The blue box around the man overlaps the left edge of the light shaft but does not contain the opening itself.
The red box encloses Goliath's lower legs, which wear ornate golden-bronze shin guards (greaves). The blue boxes contain the spear, the helmeted head and the sling; none of them shows greaves.

The red box clearly shows a large white-crested wave crashing against the side of the wooden boat. The lower blue box is centred on the boat hull. Its left edge catches some spray from the same wave, but only as a minor fringe, not a distinct instance. The upper blue box shows the robed figure standing, with calm sea behind him.
The red box frames Goliath's head, and a golden brass helmet is plainly visible on it. The blue boxes hold a sling, a spear, and the bronze greaves on his legs. None of them contains a helmet.

The red box shows the sling hanging from David's hand: the cords and the pouch holding a stone are clearly visible. The blue boxes contain Goliath's spear, his helmeted head, and his armored greaves and legs. None of them contains a sling.

The red box contains the full length of the tall spear Goliath holds, from its metal tip down to its butt on the ground. None of the blue boxes contains a spear: one holds David's sling, one Goliath's helmeted head, and one his greaved legs. The spears carried by the background soldiers fall outside every box.

Red box contains white linen cloth draped over a stone slab inside the tomb, clearly the grave clothes lying by themselves. Blue boxes show the sun, three spice jars, and the rolled-away stone; the large stone box overlaps the right edge of the cloth slightly, but its main content is the stone, not the linen.

The red box contains the bearded prophet in robes with his arms raised in prayer, standing beside the stone altar. That fits Elijah praying. The blue boxes contain the fire, the wood and sacrifice, and the stone altar. None of them contains Elijah.

The red boxes surround the jars and vessels the three women carry, which in this scene hold the spices they brought to the tomb. An adult would reasonably recognise these containers as the spices. The blue boxes show the rising sun, the burial cloth on the stone slab, and the rolled-away stone; none contains spice vessels.

The red box contains the large round boulder rolled beside the tomb entrance, which is clearly the stone that was rolled away. The blue boxes contain the sun, three ointment jars, and the stone bench with grave cloths. The bench is stone but is not the rolled-away stone.

The red box frames the stacked stone altar beneath the fire, which is clearly recognisable as a stone altar, though the exact count of twelve stones is not distinct. The blue boxes cover the prophet, the column of fire, and the wood on top of the altar. The prophet's box slightly overlaps the altar's left edge, but no blue box primarily contains the altar.

The red box contains the bright sun low on the horizon, glowing above the city, and an adult would recognise it as the rising sun. The blue boxes contain three jars, the burial cloth on the stone slab, and the rolled-away stone. None of them shows a sun.

The red box tightly frames the stacked logs on top of the stone altar, beneath the flames, and they are recognisable as wood. The fire box's lower edge and the altar-stones box's upper edge overlap slightly with the woodpile. However, the fire box mainly shows flames and the other box mainly shows stones. Neither blue box clearly contains the wood as its own subject.

The red box contains a crowned woman in an ornate royal gown and cape, clearly recognisable as Queen Esther in royal apparel. One blue box shows the king's golden scepter, with a female attendant partly visible in the background. That attendant wears simpler clothing and no crown, so she does not read as the queen. The other blue box shows the throne armrest, the king's hand and a vase of lilies.

The red box contains the golden sceptre the king is holding: a gold shaft topped with an ornate orb, plainly recognisable. The left blue box contains the queen and the right blue box contains the throne side, part of a vase and lilies. Neither blue box contains a sceptre.

The red box contains the ornate golden throne armrest and side panel, with a lion relief, on which the king rests his hand. It is clearly recognisable as the throne. The blue boxes show the queen, and the scepter with background figures; neither contains a throne.

The red box frames the large column of fire descending onto the altar, clearly recognisable as the fire of the LORD falling. The blue boxes contain the prophet with raised arms, the wood and sacrifice on top of the altar, and the stone altar itself. The sacrifice box catches only the lower edge of the flames where it overlaps the red box, so it does not clearly show the falling fire as a separate object.

The red box contains a brown ceramic jug/jar on the ground, which fits the oil-and-wine vessel from the Good Samaritan story. The blue boxes show a donkey, a bandaged arm and two travelers walking away. None of them contains a jar.

The red box clearly shows a saddled donkey standing beside the Samaritan, which is his own beast. The blue boxes contain two travelers walking away, a clay jug, and a bandaged arm. None of them shows an animal.

Red box shows the injured man's arm being wrapped with a white bandage, which clearly depicts wounds being bound up. The blue boxes contain a donkey, a clay jug, and two travelers walking away, and none of them show wounds being bound.

The red box shows two robed men walking away along the road toward the city, matching the priest and Levite who passed by on the other side in the Good Samaritan parable. The blue boxes contain a donkey, an oil jar and a bandaged arm, so none of them shows the passing men.

The red box clearly contains a gnarled olive tree with a thick twisted trunk and silvery-green leaves, on the hillside overlooking the city. One blue box holds the Temple building and the other holds the city walls. Neither contains an olive tree as its subject; only incidental distant vegetation appears below the walls.

The red box frames the gleaming temple sanctuary building, which is clearly recognisable. The left blue box shows an olive tree and distant city. The right blue box shows the massive stone retaining walls of the temple mount below the temple, not the temple building itself.

The red box clearly shows several robed mariners standing on the ship's deck. The top blue box encloses the whole ship, including additional mariners near the bow to the left of the red box, so a blue outline also clearly contains mariners. The other blue boxes show the sea creature and Jonah underwater, not mariners.

The red box clearly shows a bearded man in robes, underwater and being swallowed by the great fish, reaching out: Jonah cast into the sea. The large blue box targets the whale; it overlaps part of Jonah only because of the shared area with the red box. The boat boxes contain sailors still aboard, not a man cast into the sea.

The red box contains three bearded men in robes with crossed arms and scowling expressions, which reads clearly as Joseph's jealous brothers. The blue boxes contain Joseph in his ornate coat holding a lamb, the lamb itself, and sheep. None of the blue boxes contains the brothers.

The red box clearly shows the sailing ship carrying sailors on the stormy sea, which is the ship bound for Tarshish in the Jonah story. However, a small blue box sits inside the red box over the ship's sail, railing and sailors. It is part of the same ship, so a player tapping the ship there would be marked wrong. The large blue box (the whale) and the medium blue box (Jonah) do not contain a ship.

The red outline clearly contains the huge fish/whale-like sea creature, with its eye, head, and gaping toothed mouth. The large blue box is centred on the man being swallowed (Jonah). It overlaps part of the fish's open mouth, but it does not contain a separate great fish. The upper blue boxes show the boat and sailors. No other fish appears.

The red outline frames the long, massive crenellated stone city walls with towers and gates, so they are clearly recognisable. One blue box frames the Temple building; its bottom edge only slightly clips the tops of the wall towers, in an area the red box also covers. The other blue box shows the olive tree, the traveler and the distant city, not the walls.

The red box frames the young man's ornate, deep-blue robe with gold embroidery, which is recognisable as Joseph's coat. The blue boxes contain sheep, a lamb, and the brothers in plain striped and dull robes. The lamb box overlaps part of the coat, but its subject is the lamb. The brothers' garments are ordinary robes rather than the distinctive coat.

The red box clearly contains several sheep with white fleece. The blue boxes contain Moses, his staff, and the wall of water with part of a camel's load. None of the blue boxes contains a sheep. Other sheep, such as the one at bottom right, fall outside every box.

The red box contains the robed, bearded figure holding a staff aloft with his other arm outstretched toward the sea, which is clearly Moses. The blue boxes contain only part of the staff and his raised hand, the wall of water, and sheep, so none shows the full figure of Moses.

Red box contains the swaddled infant held by Mary. The manger blue box overlaps slightly at the bottom of the baby's wrappings but mainly shows the hay-filled manger and cloth, not the babe itself. The other blue boxes show the star, the town, and a lamb.

The red box contains the hillside town with lit stone buildings in the night background, which is clearly Bethlehem. The blue boxes contain the star, the baby, the manger and a lamb. None of them shows a town.

All three red boxes clearly contain sheep: the flock at left, the lamb Joseph holds, and the grazing sheep at lower right. The blue boxes also clearly contain sheep. The large left blue box encloses the held lamb. The right blue box encloses the grazing sheep and the sheep behind the brothers. A player tapping these sheep could be marked wrong.

The red outline clearly shows the wooden staff that Moses holds aloft. However, the large blue outline around Moses overlaps the red one, and most of the rod, including his gripping hand and the lower shaft, also falls inside that blue box. A tap on the rod could therefore register as wrong.

The red box contains the bright Star of Bethlehem, a four-pointed shining star in the night sky. The blue boxes contain the town of Bethlehem, the baby, the manger and a lamb. The star's light ray extends slightly below the red box toward the town, but no blue box clearly contains a star.

The red outline clearly contains a white lamb lying in the straw, which is recognisable as a sheep. The blue outlines contain the star, the town (with part of a donkey's head at its edge), the baby, and the manger; none contains a sheep. The other sheep at the upper left lies outside every outline.

The red box clearly shows the towering right-hand wall of water lit by the sunset. However, the large blue box around Moses and the blue box around his staff also contain visible portions of the parted water walls: the left wave wall behind him and the distant right wall beside his outstretched arm.
Red box clearly contains two elephants walking near the ark. Blue boxes show the ark with giraffes and Noah's raised arm, the rainbow, and a dove; none contains elephants.

The 'bow God set in the cloud' is the rainbow (Genesis 9:13). The red box clearly contains the rainbow arc. The blue boxes contain the dove, the elephants and Noah with the ark and giraffes. A small part of the rainbow may extend near the dove box's area, but the rainbow is not clearly inside any blue box.

The red box clearly contains a white dove in flight against the sky. The blue boxes show the ark with Noah and giraffes, the rainbow and sky, and elephants. None of them contains a dove or another bird.

The red outline contains the wooden manger filled with straw beneath the baby, and it is clearly recognisable. The blue outlines contain the star, the town, the baby (with only a sliver of straw at the manger's top edge) and the lamb. None of them clearly shows a manger.

Red box shows people standing on the sandy shore, having reached land and helping others ashore. Blue boxes show the wrecked ship with crew still aboard and people clinging to a plank in the water, so neither shows people safe on land.

The red box contains a large sailing ship striking the rocks amid crashing waves, with a torn sail and debris, so it reads clearly as a ship breaking apart. One blue box shows people on the shore. The other shows a floating wooden plank or beam with swimmers holding on. It is wreckage, not a ship, so neither blue box contains a ship breaking apart.

The red box frames the window opening, where a sunlit city with stone walls and towers is clearly visible outside, matching 'the city of Jerusalem outside'. Every blue box contains a flame above a person's head (tongues of fire), not the city. The blue box overlapping the red one near the window holds a flame over the man's head, not the cityscape.

The red box clearly shows the large wooden ark with its open doorway and giraffes. However, the ark's long hull continues to the right through the large blue box (under the rainbow) and behind the elephants in the lower blue box, so blue outlines also contain substantial parts of the ark.

The red box contains the elderly bearded man in a dark robe running forward with outstretched arms, which clearly reads as the father running to his son. The blue boxes show the women and onlookers at left, the ragged son seen from behind, and the son's bare feet. None of them shows the father.

The red outline clearly contains a large broken wooden plank floating in the water, which the man and woman are clinging to. However, the upper-left blue outline, around the wrecked ship on the rocks, also appears to include splintered boards and debris floating in the water near its lower edge. That makes the answer ambiguous.

Red box contains the group of onlookers (woman, bearded man, younger person with jar) standing by the house watching the reunion. Blue boxes contain the running father, the ragged son, and the son's feet; none show the watching servants.

The red boxes each frame a small tongue of flame hovering above a person's head, which clearly depicts the cloven tongues like as of fire. The blue box on the right covers the window and city view, but it also takes in the flame above the rightmost man's head. That same flame is framed by a red box nested inside the blue box, so the blue box also clearly contains a tongue of fire.

The red box contains a walled stone city with towers and cypress trees on elevated ground beside the lake. This is clearly a city set on a hill. The blue boxes show the seated teacher figure and a hillside of wildflowers, with no city in either.

The red box contains the ragged, barefoot young man walking toward the father, which is clearly the returning son. The blue boxes show the father running to greet him, the onlooking woman and servants, and a close-up of the son's feet. The feet are only a part of the son, not a distinct instance of him, so no blue box clearly shows the returning son as its own object.

The red outline tightly frames the son's dirty bare feet and lower legs, which are clearly recognisable. However, the large blue outline around the whole son fully encloses the red region, so it also contains the same bare feet. The father wears sandals, and the background figures' feet are not shown bare.

The red box clearly contains the central robed, bearded teaching figure seated on the hillside, recognisable as Jesus. One blue box overlaps his lower legs and feet, but it mainly shows wildflowers and the back of a listener's head, so it does not clearly contain the figure. The other blue box contains only a distant stone town.

The upper red box clearly contains a golden menorah, a multi-branched candlestick with lit candles. The lower red box shows another lit golden candlestick or lampstand. The blue boxes contain pillars with winged-creature reliefs and the robed king, none of which is a candlestick. The large blue box around the king partially overlaps the lower red box, but it does not clearly frame a candlestick.

The red outline clearly contains wildflowers (purple, yellow and white blooms) on the hillside. The blue outline around the seated teacher extends down over the same flower patch, with yellow and purple flowers visible near his feet and along its left edge. So a blue area also clearly contains flowers of the field. The second blue box, around the town, does not.

The red box contains the crowned king in blue and gold robes standing at the top of the steps with both arms raised toward the sky, which is clearly Solomon spreading his hands toward heaven. The blue boxes show pillars, winged lion reliefs, a menorah and a flame. One pillar box overlaps part of the king's body, but it does not depict a separate figure with raised hands.

Both red boxes clearly show carved winged sphinx/cherub figures on the golden pillars. However, the blue box around the central pillar (and the large blue box around the king, which overlaps it) also contains a clearly visible carved winged cherub/sphinx of the same kind, making the answer ambiguous.

All three red boxes clearly frame tall golden columns (left, center and right pillars). However, the blue boxes overlap pillar surfaces. The two winged-lion relief boxes sit entirely on the left and right pillars, and the large blue box around the king includes much of the center pillar. Taps on those areas land on a pillar but could be scored as wrong.
